audit_findings.title: 2025 capital spending was largely financed through finance leases, bypassing the capex line and inflating the anchor's trend endpoint
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed: $1,389m of finance-lease right-of-use assets obtained in 2025, against $21m (2024) and $30m (2023); reported capex $1,282m; finance-lease principal paid $346m in 2025 (including the $315m December Facility Lease payment) vs $30m in 2024. Computed: capitalising the 2025 ROU additions takes 2025 capex to ~$2,671m and 2025 owner earnings from $1,561m to roughly $170m — close to the $29.8m 2024 trough.
audit_findings.mechanism: Enters the capex deduction in the 2025 owner-earnings figure, therefore the endpoint of the log trend fitted through 2016-2025, therefore the $364.7m anchor under MIN(trend, latest) and every scenario value and buy_below.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recognized $ 1.4 billion in right-of-use assets and lease liabilities primarily associated with recently commenced leases, as discussed below.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated error of consistency, not a possibility. The filing shows productive plant reaching service through finance leases in 2025 at a scale (~$1.4bn) larger than the entire reported capex line, and the prior-year comparatives confirm the substitution is concentrated in the anchor year rather than being a stable feature of the series — precisely the pattern that corrupts a fitted endpoint. Correcting it lowers 2025 owner earnings by roughly 89 percent and pulls the trend and the anchor down with it. The direction is important for the reader: this widens the gap between the $8.55 base value and the $146 price rather than closing it, so it cannot reverse the do-not-buy conclusion, but it materially changes the number the board publishes and is the largest single identified defect in the anchor year.
audit_findings.action: Re-run 4b for 2025 with finance-lease ROU additions treated as capital expenditure (or, in the alternative, deduct finance-lease principal payments), read the leases note in each of the 2016-2024 10-Ks to apply the same convention across the series, re-fit the trend in 4d, and record the chosen convention and its reasoning in PIPELINE.md.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated-basis owner earnings and cash are divided by the parent's share count alone (HSG minority)
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed: net income attributable to non-controlling interest $146m in 2025 (8.4% of $1,742m consolidated net income), $86m in 2024, $67m in 2023; NCI equity $500m at 31-Dec-2025 and $567m at 30-Jun-2026; depreciation $1,237m and capex $1,282m are consolidated. Cash split between wholly-owned and partly-owned subsidiaries: not disclosed — unquantified. 61% of consolidated cash held outside the US; $1.9bn of indefinitely reinvested foreign earnings.
audit_findings.mechanism: The owner-earnings numerator (if consolidated D&A and capex are paired with attributable net income, or consolidated income is divided by parent shares) and the $2,504m cash added in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The non-controlling interest as recorded on the consolidated financial statements represents amounts attributable to the minority shareholders of less-than-wholly-owned consolidated subsidiaries, including Hemlock Semiconductor Group (“HSG”) and other subsidiaries primarily within our Optical Communications segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The basis mismatch is a real hazard and the minority claim is quantified at roughly 8-9 percent of consolidated earnings, which would be worth on the order of $0.7 per share against the $8.55 base. What the record cannot settle is whether an error actually exists: the run material supplied here does not show which basis 4b used for each year's numerator and add-backs, and if it was attributable throughout with attributable-share add-backs there is no error at all. The cash leg is genuinely unquantifiable from the filings — Corning does not disclose cash by subsidiary — so the repatriation and minority haircuts can only be estimated, not computed. Either way the scale is too small to move a valuation that sits seventeen times below the traded price.
audit_findings.action: Pull the 4b extraction record and confirm, year by year, the basis of the numerator and of the D&A and capex add-backs; make them consistent in one direction and note it. For the bridge, either apply the NCI ownership percentage to cash as an explicit stated proxy or mark the split as undisclosed, and state the repatriation-tax assumption on the $1.9bn of indefinitely reinvested earnings rather than leaving it implicit.

audit_findings.title: Government subsidies flatter both the earnings numerator and the capex deduction, and are policy-contingent with a recapture clause
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025: $172m of 45X credits through cost of sales, $87m of 48D credits through operating expenses, $323m of 48D credits against asset carrying value (of which $318m reduced finance-lease ROU assets — $189m facility, $129m equipment), $84m of 48C credits earned. Filed 2024 comparative: $83m of 45X only; 2024 48D credits 'not material'. So ~$259m of income-statement credits equal ~17% of the $1,561m 2025 owner-earnings figure, and a further ~$323m understates capital consumed.
audit_findings.mechanism: Raises the owner-earnings numerator through cost of sales and operating expenses, and lowers the recorded capital cost that the capex deduction is taken from — both feeding the 2025 endpoint and therefore the fitted trend and the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company placed in service qualified property, resulting in the recognition of $ 323 million of 48D credits that reduced the carrying value of the related asset and $ 87 million of 48D credits that were recognized as a reduction of operating expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: This is demonstrated from the filing and it compounds finding 1, because the asset-side credits attach to the same leased solar assets. The comparability problem is the sharper one: the 2025 endpoint carries roughly $259m of P&L credits against essentially none in 2024 and 2023, so part of the apparent 2025 recovery is a change in statutory support rather than in the business. Grossing up would reduce 2025 owner earnings by a sixth on the P&L side alone before any capital-cost adjustment. The separate policy question — that 48D credits are subject to five-year recapture and the whole regime is a creature of the IRA and CHIPS Acts as amended — is forward-looking and belongs in the bear case rather than in the historic series, but it means the credits cannot be extrapolated as a durable rate.
audit_findings.action: Recompute 2025, 2024 and 2023 owner earnings gross of all P&L credits and with the asset-side credits added back to capital cost, taking care not to double-count the $323m asset-side 48D against the $318m ROU reduction, and re-fit the trend. Separately, specify in the bear case whether credits are assumed to lapse, and record the ruling.

audit_findings.title: 2025 operating cash flow was lifted by non-recurring customer prepayments and incentive receipts, not by trading
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 cash-flow lines: customer deposits and government incentives +$268m and deferred income -$58m (net +$210m), against -$33m net in 2024; $490m of new customer-contract deposits and $119m of new deferred-revenue consideration received; customer deposits $1.5bn and deferred revenue $775m at 31-Dec-2025. At 30-Jun-2026 contract liabilities total $2,709m ($465m current, $2,244m non-current) against the $2,504m of cash added in the bridge, which includes the $1.0bn customer deposit received in Q2 2026. Computed: cash contributes $2,504m/892.1m = $2.81 per share of the $8.55 base; excluding the $1.0bn deposit alone gives $7.43.
audit_findings.mechanism: The owner-earnings numerator, if 4b derived it from operating cash flow; and, separately and more materially, the cash-and-STI leg of the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company received $ 490 million relating to new customer contracts.
audit_findings.explanation: Two distinct issues sit inside this finding and they do not carry equal weight. The cash-flow-statement effect on 2025 owner earnings is only about $210m net on the face of the filing — not the $756m improvement management attributes to several causes — and it may not enter at all, because a Buffett-frame numerator built from net income plus D&A less capex never touches working-capital swings; the record supplied does not establish which construction 4b used. The bridge effect is computable and larger: a third of the base value per share is cash, $1.0bn of which arrived as a non-refundable customer prepayment in the quarter ending on the very balance-sheet date used, against product to be delivered through 2029 and against capacity still being built to deliver it, while the offsetting $2.7bn of contract liabilities is not deducted anywhere. One correction to the finding as written: the $1.0bn deposit is a Q2 2026 event and therefore cannot be inside the FY2016-FY2025 series, so it is not double-counted in the anchor; any double count is between the bridge cash and the bull-case narrative.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether 4b's numerator is cash-flow or net-income derived; if cash-flow derived, strip the customer-deposit, government-incentive and deferred-income lines from every year and re-fit. Separately, rule in PIPELINE.md on whether prepaid customer cash belongs in the bridge cash add, and run 4d with and without the $1.0bn deposit ($8.55 versus $7.43 base) so the owner sees the sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: A large, recurring, cash hedging economic flow is routed through investing activities, outside owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed investing lines: realized gains on translated earnings contracts and other +$304m (2025), +$279m (2024), +$326m (2023); premiums paid on hedging contracts -$122m, -$98m, -$9m — net +$182m, +$181m and +$317m respectively. Income statement: translated earnings contract gain of $150m in 2025, of which $146m is unrealized mark-to-market; $10.8bn of translated-earnings notional at year-end. Constant-currency reconciling adjustment $665m at income-before-tax in 2025.
audit_findings.mechanism: The owner-earnings numerator: whether a non-cash mark was left in, and whether a recurring realized cash result was left out.
audit_findings.evidence: (2) For the year ended December 31, 2025, amount excludes $5 million gain related to forward contracts designated as a net investment hedge, which was recorded in accumulated other comprehensive loss on the consolidated balance sheets and reflected within investing activities on the consolidated statements of cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure is real and recurring — roughly $180m a year of cash hedge result sitting in investing activities across three consecutive years — but the direction of any error cannot be determined from the record, because the run material does not show which hedge lines 4b took into each year. If the $146m unrealized mark was retained, owner earnings are overstated by about 9 percent of the 2025 figure; if the realized cash result was excluded, they are understated by a similar order. Either error is roughly a tenth of the anchor year, well short of what would change a conclusion drawn against a seventeen-fold price gap, which is why this is an open question rather than a demonstrated material defect. The related warning is worth acting on independently: segment results are struck at management-set constant-currency rates that differ from GAAP by $665m at the pre-tax line in 2025, so any segment-level figure leaking into the series would be a genuine error.
audit_findings.action: Retrieve the 4b per-year line inventory and confirm three things: that the $146m unrealized translated-earnings gain was purged, whether the realized hedge result net of premiums was included or excluded, and that every year in the series was built from consolidated GAAP statements rather than segment or core tables. Record the hedge convention in PIPELINE.md so it is applied consistently on refresh.

audit_findings.title: The share denominator includes post-period warrant shares whose earnings and exercise proceeds are absent from the numerator and bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed: 857,948,109 shares outstanding at 30-Jan-2026; weighted-average diluted 875m in Q2 2026; 18m warrant shares issued 6-May-2026 (15m Traditional at $180.00, 3m Pre-Funded at $0.0001); 2.5m options outstanding at a $24.07 weighted-average exercise price; $500m of Pre-Funded Warrant proceeds received in Q2 2026 and therefore already inside the $2,504m bridge cash. Computed: the 18m warrant shares are 2.0% of the 892.1m denominator, worth about $0.17 per share on the $8.55 base; the unpaired Traditional Warrant strike proceeds are ~$2,700m, or $3.03 per share, and the option proceeds ~$61m, or $0.07.
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator in value per share, and the cash leg of the bridge that the ceiling method leaves unpaired.
audit_findings.evidence: There were 857,948,109 shares of common stock outstanding as of January 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The inconsistency is demonstrated — shares counted, strike cash not — but it runs against the valuation, not for it, because the ceiling denominator is deliberately conservative. Its direct cost is small, about two percent of the denominator, consistent with the 892.1m figure sitting just under two percent above the company's own diluted 875m. What makes this uncertain rather than immaterial is the other side: pairing the 15m Traditional Warrant shares with their $2.7bn of proceeds would add roughly $3.03 per share, about 35 percent of the base value. That pairing is not obviously right either, since at a $180 strike against an $8.55 owner-earnings value the warrants are deep out of the money and would never be exercised, which argues for excluding both the shares and the cash. The two coherent treatments differ by an amount that matters to the published number while leaving the valuation an order of magnitude below the $146 price. The Pre-Funded Warrant needs no adjustment: its $500m is already in the bridge cash.
audit_findings.action: Choose one treatment — exclude both the 15m shares and the strike cash, or include both — document the ruling in PIPELINE.md, and re-run 4d each way so the owner sees the spread. Separately, reconcile the 12/31/2025 option/RSU/PSU inventory against the 857,948,109 cover-page count, netting the ~$23m of post-year-end option exercises and the 1.33m of vest-related withholdings, and report the net share-count error rather than assuming the offsets cancel.
